body:
10-year facility expected to strengthen local-currency funding for energy, transport, healthcare, digital infrastructure

The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, has committed $50 million in long-term subordinated debt to Infrastructure Credit Guarantee Company Plc (InfraCredit), in a move aimed at expanding the company’s capacity to finance infrastructure projects across Nigeria.

The 10-year unsecured facility, formalised in Lagos, will be disbursed in two equal tranches of $25 million. The financing is expected to strengthen InfraCredit’s capital base and enable the company to support a growing pipeline of infrastructure transactions while helping mobilise more long-term naira funding for projects in critical sectors of the economy.

The facility will support investments spanning renewable energy, climate-smart agriculture, telecommunications, digital infrastructure, healthcare and transportation, as well as other projects linked to sustainable economic growth.

The IFC investment is backed by the International Development Association Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility and the Concessional Capital Window, reflecting the role of development finance institutions in supporting infrastructure financing and domestic capital-market development in emerging economies.

InfraCredit provides credit guarantees for infrastructure-related debt transactions, helping project developers access long-term financing while encouraging domestic institutional investors to participate in the market.

The company said the additional capital would enhance its ability to attract domestic institutional investment into infrastructure projects that require long-term financing.

It added that the transaction underscored growing support from international development finance institutions for its efforts to deepen Nigeria’s domestic debt capital market and increase the availability of long-term local-currency financing.

Expanding development finance support

The IFC facility forms part of a broader network of support that InfraCredit has received from development finance institutions and other development partners.

According to the company, its partners have provided different forms of capital and risk-sharing support, including equity investments, subordinated debt, portfolio risk-sharing mechanisms, counter-guarantees, first-loss capital, specialised financing facilities and technical assistance.

InfraCredit said the combination of these instruments had helped strengthen its financial leverage while enabling it to develop new financing structures and co-financing platforms for infrastructure projects.

The company began operations in 2017 and said it has since facilitated more than N600 billion in long-term local-currency financing for 28 infrastructure projects.

It has also supported 14 first-time issuers in accessing Nigeria’s domestic debt capital market, helping broaden participation in the market and create new opportunities for infrastructure developers to raise funds locally.

Among the transactions supported by InfraCredit are deals that helped establish new benchmarks in Nigeria’s local bond market, including the country’s first 15-year green infrastructure bond.

InfraCredit-guaranteed transactions have also enabled corporate bond maturities to extend to as much as 20 years, providing infrastructure developers with access to financing over periods more closely aligned with the long-term nature of infrastructure assets.

The company said its guaranteed infrastructure bonds had attracted substantial participation from domestic institutional investors, including 20 of Nigeria’s 25 Pension Fund Administrators.

IFC: facility will help mobilise domestic capital

IFC’s Financial Institutions Group Director for Africa, Aliou Maiga, said the investment would help strengthen Nigeria’s infrastructure financing ecosystem by supporting the mobilisation of domestic resources.

“By supporting InfraCredit’s institutional capacity, we are helping mobilise domestic resources for infrastructure investments that can drive economic growth, job creation and sustainable development across key sectors of the Nigerian economy,” Maiga said.

He said IFC was pleased to deepen its partnership with InfraCredit as the company continued to contribute to the development of Nigeria’s local capital markets.

InfraCredit cites growing pipeline

The Chief Executive Officer of InfraCredit, Chinua Azubike, said strengthening the company’s institutional capacity had become increasingly important as its transaction pipeline expanded and its financing products evolved.

According to him, the IFC facility would improve InfraCredit’s ability to mobilise long-term domestic capital for infrastructure projects.

Azubike described the investment as evidence of continued confidence from international development finance institutions in InfraCredit’s business model.

He also pointed to the range of development finance institutions and other partners supporting the company through different layers of its capital and risk-sharing structures.

“This breadth of support is a significant competitive advantage and reflects the maturity and resilience of our institution,” he said.

The latest financing comes as Nigeria continues to face the challenge of mobilising long-term capital for infrastructure development, particularly in sectors where projects require substantial upfront investment and extended repayment periods.

By strengthening InfraCredit’s balance sheet and guarantee capacity, the new facility is expected to support the company’s efforts to connect infrastructure developers with domestic institutional investors and deepen the role of Nigeria’s local debt capital market in financing long-term economic development.
